answers.stem_only: The request is accepted and the response is rejected, so the block is on the return path, not the inbound rule. Security groups are stateful, so the service security group already allows the response to an allowed request. The client subnet uses the default network ACL, which allows all traffic. That leaves the stateless network ACL of the service subnet: it has no outbound rule for the return traffic. Add one narrow outbound rule to the service subnet's network ACL that allows TCP on the clients' ephemeral port range (Linux range, about 32768-61000) to the client subnet CIDR only.
